title: [Audit] 🚨 Security & Anomalies
description: Mean-severity risk scoring, privileged operations, failures and newly seen identities.

config.description: Average severity weight across scoring events, on the same 0–50 scale as the weights: config change 50, key invalidation 45, failure 40, anonymous denial 35, destructive change 30, other Kibana change 25, workflow execution 10. Executions weigh least on purpose — they are the one class with unbounded cadence, and a scheduled workflow firing every minute would otherwise turn total risk back into an event count. Routine activity scores 0 and is excluded, so this is not a disguised event count — read it with Scoring events beside it.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL OR attributes.event.outcome == "failure" OR attributes.event.action IN ("invalidate_apikeys","anonymous_access_denied") OR (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY attributes.event.action, scc = attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, attributes.event.outcome, resource.attributes.service.name, et = MV_CONCAT(attributes.event.type, ",") | EVAL attributes.event.type = SPLIT(et, ","), attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change = CASE(scc, "present") | EVAL risk = CASE(attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys", 45, attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied", 35, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, 50, attributes.event.outcome == "failure", 40, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND attributes.event.action IN ("workflow_run","workflow_test","workflow_execution_cancel"), 10, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND (attributes.event.type == "deletion" OR attributes.event.action == "rule_disable"), 30, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))), 25, 0) | WHERE risk > 0 | STATS risk_total = SUM(risk * n), scoring_events = SUM(n) | EVAL mean_severity = ROUND(1.0 * risk_total / scoring_events, 1) | EVAL `Mean severity (of 50)` = mean_severity | KEEP `Mean severity (of 50)`

config.description: Security configuration changes recorded by Elasticsearch (API keys created, changed or invalidated, roles and user profiles written) — the total that the Config changes table and the event feed below draw from. Kibana's own API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account through no named key, every few seconds) is left out, as on Command Center's Privileged ops; the second line says how many such events the range held. On a range that ends now, each panel runs its query as it scrolls into view, so an event that arrives during the page load can be in one panel and not yet in another; Refresh reconciles them.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL | EVAL housekeeping = (attributes.event.action IS NOT NULL AND attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys" AND attributes.user.name IS NOT NULL AND attributes.user.name IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana") AND attributes.api_key.name IS NULL) | STATS `Config changes` = COUNT(*) WHERE NOT housekeeping, cleanups = COUNT(*) WHERE housekeeping | EVAL housekeeping_note = CASE(cleanups > 0, CONCAT(TO_STRING(cleanups), " key cleanups left out"), "no key cleanups in range") | EVAL housekeeping_note = CASE(cleanups == 0, "no cleanups in range", cleanups < 1000, CONCAT("excl. ", TO_STRING(cleanups), " cleanups"), CONCAT("excl. ", TO_STRING(FLOOR(cleanups / 1000)), ",", RIGHT(CONCAT("00", TO_STRING(cleanups % 1000)), 3), " cleanups"))

config.description: invalidate_apikeys requests in range (one request can name several keys) — legitimate rotation, or a credential being revoked in a hurry; a subset of Config changes. Kibana's own API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account through no named key, every few seconds) is left out, as on Command Center's Privileged ops; the second line says how many such events the range held. The risk scoring still weighs every invalidation, the clean-up included: it is elastic/kibana's invalidate_apikeys row in Why these identities scored.

config.title: 🚨 Config changes by identity and action · latest 9 (may be empty at 1h)
config.description: Security configuration changes grouped by identity and action, the most recently active first; in a busy range the quieter pairs are beyond the rows shown, so Events here add up to the Config changes tile only when every pair fits. Kibana's own API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account through no named key, every few seconds) is left out, as on Command Center's Privileged ops. Latest target is what the newest of those changes named (the API key, the key ids of an invalidation, the role, or the user profile), and Targets counts the different ones named across all of them: hundreds of invalidations over hundreds of keys is rotation, hundreds over one key is a loop. A profile activation names no target (it is the signed-in user's own profile), so it reads "(none named in the payload)" and 0. A key named "TaskManager: … - <id>" is one Kibana created to run a task on that identity's behalf: the id at its end is its owner's, not a name for it. The full JSON payload of every change is in the Config-change event feed at the foot of the page. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. Often empty over the default hour on a healthy project; widen the time range to see older rows.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL AND NOT (attributes.event.action IS NOT NULL AND attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys" AND attributes.user.name IS NOT NULL AND attributes.user.name IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana") AND attributes.api_key.name IS NULL) | GROK attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change """"name":"%{DATA:t_name}"""" | GROK attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change """"ids":\[%{DATA:t_ids}\]""" | GROK attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change """"id":"%{DATA:t_id}"""" | GROK attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change """"uid":"%{DATA:t_uid}"""" | EVAL target = COALESCE(t_name, REPLACE(t_ids, "\"", ""), t_id, t_uid) | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS events = COUNT(*), targets = COUNT_DISTINCT(SPLIT(target, ",")), latest = LAST(target, @timestamp), last_change = MAX(@timestamp) BY actor, action = attributes.event.action | SORT last_change DESC | EVAL actor_scope = CASE(actor IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana"), "platform", actor IN ("<anonymous>","<unauthenticated-cloud-access-token>","<unauthenticated-saml-user>","<unauthenticated-cloud-api-key>"), "unauthenticated", "tenant") | EVAL latest = REPLACE(latest, ",", ", ") | EVAL latest = CASE(LENGTH(latest) > 72, CONCAT(LEFT(latest, 71), "…"), latest) | EVAL latest = COALESCE(latest, "(none named in the payload)") | LIMIT 9 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Highest-severity actions, by how rare
config.description: The highest-severity scoring actions in range, one row per action and weight, placed by how often each happened: rarer is further left, so the top-left is rare and high-severity — look there first. Shows the top 12 by severity, rarest first within a weight; the subtitle says how many actions scored in all. On a quiet range the top 12 reach down to routine Kibana changes (weight 25), which can be frequent: rare is a position on this chart, not a filter. Each row ends with its severity weight, which the colour repeats. A failed change scores 40 whatever it changed, so it gets its own row, marked (failed). Hover a point for how many identities did it and when. Routine activity scores 0 and is not shown. Counts are what risk scoring weighs, Kibana's own API-key clean-up included, so invalidate_apikeys here can be far above the Key invalidations tile, which leaves that clean-up out.

config.title: Risk over time
config.description: Summed severity weight per interval, routine activity excluded, split by who it came from: tenant identities, Elastic platform automation, or unauthenticated requests. Spikes are clusters of privileged, failed or denied activity. The axis always spans the whole range: a blank stretch means nothing scored then, or, on a project younger than the range, that the audit stream had not started yet.

config.title: Identities by first appearance in range · latest 8
config.description: Identities ordered by their first event inside the selected range, latest first, from signal events only (query internals are left out, as on every gated panel). First seen is within the range, not ever: an identity that was already active when the range opened also shows a first-seen near its start. New reads "no" for those (first seen in the opening twelfth of the range) and "yes" otherwise; on a project whose audit history is shorter than the range, every identity reads "yes". A "yes" near the top is an identity worth a question; widen the range to tell a new identity from a returning one. Client IPs is 0 for identities whose events record no client address (the Kibana service account, platform automation). An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("cluster:monitor/main", "elastic.maintenance") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/search*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/msearch*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/scroll*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/*point_in_time" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/open_reader_context" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/esql*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:admin/esql/*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/field_caps*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/async_search/*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:admin/resolve/*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:admin/shards/search_shards" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "cluster:monitor/xpack/esql/*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("cluster:monitor/project/tags", "cluster:monitor/xpack/inference/get"))) AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_success","connection_granted") OR attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time","space_get","space_find") OR (attributes.event.action == "http_request" AND attributes.url.original IS NOT NULL AND attributes.url.original RLIKE "https?://[^/]+(/s/[^/]+)?/((internal|translations|app)/.*|api/content_management/rpc/(get|search|mget|bulkGet).*|bootstrap(-anonymous)?[.]js.*|api/(core|licensing|banners|ui_counters)/.*|api/spaces/space([?].*)?)") OR (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_get","saved_object_resolve","saved_object_find") AND attributes.kibana.saved_object.id IS NOT NULL AND attributes.kibana.saved_object.id LIKE "cloud-audit-*"))) | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), events = COUNT(*), ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(client.ip) BY actor | SORT first_seen DESC | EVAL actor_scope = CASE(actor IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana"), "platform", actor IN ("<anonymous>","<unauthenticated-cloud-access-token>","<unauthenticated-saml-user>","<unauthenticated-cloud-api-key>"), "unauthenticated", "tenant") | EVAL new_in_range = CASE(TO_LONG(first_seen) - TO_LONG(TO_DATETIME(?_tstart)) > (TO_LONG(TO_DATETIME(?_tend)) - TO_LONG(TO_DATETIME(?_tstart))) / 12, "yes", "no") | LIMIT 8 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Risk leaderboard — top 10 identities by total severity
config.description: Identities ranked by total accumulated severity, so sustained behaviour outranks a single high-severity event; only the top of the ranking fits the panel. Scope separates tenant identities from Elastic platform automation and unauthenticated requests — without it elastic.maintenance can top this table, because Elastic platform automation performs routine security config changes itself. Privileged counts the identity's security config changes the way the Config changes tile does, Kibana's own API-key clean-up left out; Risk total still includes that clean-up. Identity is the email for a person and the key name for a named API key. To follow one person, pick them in the Person (email) control; the pin carries to Actor 360. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.

config.title: Why these identities scored — top 10 risky actions, with their weight
config.description: The receipts behind the leaderboard: the identity and action pairs that contributed the most risk, with what each action weighed, how many times it happened, and when it last did. Risk total is weight × events, the same quantity the leaderboard sums. Only the largest contributions fit the panel, so a rare action can be missing here: Highest-severity actions, by how rare lists the actions by severity instead. To follow one person, pick them in the Person (email) control; the pin carries to Actor 360. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.

resource.attributes.service.name, et = MV_CONCAT(attributes.event.type, ",") | EVAL attributes.event.type = SPLIT(et, ","), attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change = CASE(scc, "present") | EVAL risk = CASE(attributes.event.action == "invalidate_apikeys", 45, attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied", 35, attributes.elasticsearch.audit.security_config_change IS NOT NULL, 50, attributes.event.outcome == "failure", 40, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND attributes.event.action IN ("workflow_run","workflow_test","workflow_execution_cancel"), 10, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) AND (attributes.event.type == "deletion" OR attributes.event.action == "rule_disable"), 30, (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))), 25, 0) | WHERE risk > 0 | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | EVAL actor_scope = CASE(actor IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana"), "platform", actor IN ("<anonymous>","<unauthenticated-cloud-access-token>","<unauthenticated-saml-user>","<unauthenticated-cloud-api-key>"), "unauthenticated", "tenant") | STATS events = SUM(n), risk_total = SUM(risk * n), last_seen = MAX(last_ts) BY actor, actor_scope, action = attributes.event.action, weight = risk | SORT risk_total DESC | LIMIT 10 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Top 8 failures and denials by identity (empty = good)
config.description: Failed and denied operations grouped by identity, action and source IP, the most frequent first; only the top rows fit the panel. These are the events the Failures tile counts (every denial and failed sign-in carries a failure outcome), and the Anonymous denials tile is their anonymous_access_denied rows. Scope separates unauthenticated probes from tenant identities and Elastic platform automation. API keys and native users (elastic, admin) carry no email, so an Identity that is not an email does not mean an external probe — read Scope. To follow one person, pick them in the Person (email) control; the pin carries to Actor 360. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. An empty panel means nothing matched in the time range, which is the healthy state; any row here is worth reading.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.outcome == "failure" OR attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_failed","realm_authentication_failed","anonymous_access_denied") | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>") | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY actor, action = attributes.event.action, ip = client.ip | SORT events DESC | EVAL actor_scope = CASE(actor IN ("elastic.maintenance","autoscaling","elasticsearch-controller","elastic/fleet-server","elastic/kibana"), "platform", actor IN ("<anonymous>","<unauthenticated-cloud-access-token>","<unauthenticated-saml-user>","<unauthenticated-cloud-api-key>"), "unauthenticated", "tenant") | LIMIT 8 | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Config-change event feed · newest 1,000 at most (may be empty at 1h)
config.description: Every security configuration change the Config changes tile counts, as its own event, newest first, with the payload in full; expand a row to read a long one. Kibana's own API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account through no named key, every few seconds) is left out, as on Command Center's Privileged ops. Discover returns at most the newest 1,000 events, and its result count is that cap rather than the total: when it reads 1,000, the Config changes tile at the top has the total. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. Often empty over the default hour on a healthy project; widen the time range to see older rows.

config.title: Mutation feed · newest 1,000 at most
config.description: Creates, updates and deletes across Kibana and Elasticsearch security config, newest first. Object is what the change named: the saved object or feature object for a Kibana change; for an Elasticsearch security change, the API key's name, the key ids of an invalidation, the role or the profile, with its full JSON payload under Message. Kibana's own API-key clean-up (invalidate_apikeys by the elastic/kibana service account through no named key, every few seconds) is left out, as on Command Center's Privileged ops. Discover returns at most the newest 1,000 events, and its result count is that cap rather than the total. To reach older events, narrow the time range. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.
